extracted.intended_audience: Depositors (patent applicants, researchers, patent agents) and staff submitting or managing biological-material deposits under the Budapest Treaty at national/international culture collections
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and technical requirements for depositing biological material (microorganisms, plasmids, cell lines, viruses, etc.) with international/national culture collections under the Budapest Treaty, including form/quantity, viability testing, administrative forms, notifications, furnishing of samples, fees, and depositor obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance limited to material preservable without significant change
rubrics_metrics.description: Strains that may be cultivated and preserved under technically feasible conditions, without inducing significant changes in their characteristics, can be accepted. Exceptionally, collections may accept deposits that cannot be conserved other than by active culture, by case-by-case negotiation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collections may negotiate case-by-case acceptance and fees for material requiring active culture; depositaries reserve right to refuse deposits that are hazardous or received in bad condition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to refuse hazardous or unsuitable deposits
rubrics_metrics.description: Collections reserve their right to refuse a deposit of biological material whose manipulation or conservation involves hazards deemed to be excessive, or if they receive the material in a bad condition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depositors should provide accurate hazard/species information and expect refusal if safety or sample quality is inadequate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Addressing deposits to the appropriate collection
rubrics_metrics.description: All deposits should be addressed directly to the appropriate BCCMTM collection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact details and collection-specific instructions are provided by each collection; follow collection-specific submission pathways.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and quantity — bacteria, filamentous fungi, yeasts, actinomycetes (BCCM)
rubrics_metrics.description: The depositor must supply 23 ampoules with freeze-dried cells of the same batch. If unable to provide 23 ampoules, at least 3 ampoules of the same batch. If not available freeze-dried, supply 3 vials of frozen cultures or 3 active cultures of the same batch.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One or more ampoules/vials/active cultures will be tested for viability and used to prepare a stock of 20 cryopreserved samples. BCCMTM can prepare 20 freeze-dried samples for an additional fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and quantity — arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi (BCCM)
rubrics_metrics.description: Optimally supply 2 in vitro (monoxenic) cultures of the same batch. Otherwise supply an inoculum containing propagules (spores and/or mycorrhizal root fragments) from a single monosporal culture; mixtures only accepted if derived from the same mother monosporal culture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upon request BCCM/MUCL may attempt to grow AMF under in vitro monoxenic culture for an additional fee. Note: trap plant cultures cannot assess purity beyond Glomeromycota due to non-aseptic conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and quantity — plasmids in bacterial host (BCCM)
rubrics_metrics.description: Depositor must supply three active, freeze-dried or frozen cultures of the same batch; one or more will be subjected to a viability test and used for cryopreserved stock preparation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the recommended host strain is not available at the depositary, the depositor is encouraged to deposit a plasmid-carrying culture or furnish the host strain (additional fees and long-term storage charges may apply).

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and quantity — plasmids as isolated material (BCCM)
rubrics_metrics.description: Samples must be supplied freeze-dried, frozen, or precipitated in alcohol. A minimum of 2 x 20 micrograms must be furnished. The plasmid DNA must have sufficient purity to ensure successful transformation. The recommended bacterial host strain must be stated and, if not available at the depositary, furnished by the depositor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the host must be furnished by the depositor, storage of the host strain for at least 30 years will be charged separately; viability testing for isolated genetic material includes transformation of the suitable host and confirmation by expected restriction fragments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and quantity — human and animal cells, hybridomas (BCCM)
rubrics_metrics.description: Animal and human cell cultures or hybridomas must be checked for contaminants before submission. Mass frozen cultures must contain at least 4 x 10^6 viable cells per vial. At least 12 samples of the same batch in well-sealed, clearly marked 1–2 ml cryotubes (±12 mm diameter) must be supplied; one or more will be subjected to a viability test.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BCCM/LMBP may refuse deposit when cultures are thawed upon arrival. Viability testing includes mycoplasma contamination testing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative forms when depositor cannot meet ideal packaging (BCCM/IDAC)
rubrics_metrics.description: If depositor cannot supply freeze-dried material, collections may accept frozen samples or active cultures (sometimes with minimum numbers) or negotiate case-by-case; depositaries may prepare preserved material for an additional fee and will return a portion to depositor for verification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If preserved material prepared by the depositary is viable but displays altered properties, a new deposit must be made and the original deposit date will be void; depositors are urged to supply properly prepared preserved material from their labs to avoid this.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum quantities — IDAC (Canada)
rubrics_metrics.description: Microorganisms: 10 frozen (0.5 ml each) or freeze-dried samples. Plasmids/vectors not in host: 25 vials (min. 100 ng each). Animal viruses: 25 frozen (1 ml each) or freeze-dried samples. Cell lines and hybridomas: 25 frozen samples (2–6 million cells each).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are the IDAC-specified minima; other collections have different minima (see collection-specific entries).

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum quantities — NBIMCC (Bulgaria)
rubrics_metrics.description: Bacteria and fungi should be deposited as three active cultures. Lyophilized cultures accepted but must have at least 10 samples. Animal cell lines and hybridomas: 12 frozen cryotubes each containing minimum 5 x 10^6 cells. Animal viruses: 20 frozen or freeze-dried samples. Plant viruses: at least 5 g fresh infected leaves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the collection-specific sample numbers and formats; lyophilized forms often require larger numbers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time required for viability testing (collection-specific minima)
rubrics_metrics.description: Collections publish minimum periods for viability testing by material type (examples: BCCM — bacteria 3 days, fungi 3 days, yeasts 2 days, AMF 30 days, plasmids ±1 week, human/animal cells ±3 weeks; NBIMCC — bacteria/yeasts/plasmid 3–14 days, fungi 5–21 days, cell lines 7–14 days, viruses 30+ days; IDAC — bacteria 3–7 days, fungi/yeasts 7–10 days, cell lines/plasmids/phages 7–10 days, animal viruses 30+ days).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Viability testing may take longer for certain organisms; specific tests may include growth, transformation, restriction analysis, and mycoplasma testing. Depositors should anticipate and plan for possible extended testing times.

rubrics_metrics.name: Viability test content for genetic material and cell lines
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'viability test' for plasmids includes preparation of plasmid DNA and restriction enzyme analysis by gel electrophoresis; for isolated genetic material, viability implies transformation of a suitable host with confirmation of expected fragments. For human/animal cells, viability testing includes testing for mycoplasma contamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collections may reject deposits if viability tests fail; for isolated genetic material, transformation success is the criterion of viability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depositor checks and renewal of stocks (BCCM/others)
rubrics_metrics.description: At the time of deposit, the collection prepares its own cryopreserved and depending on form, freeze-dried batch; the depositor is provided with one sample to check authenticity. To renew depleted stocks, collections will prepare new batches starting from one sample of the previous batch; for some materials (renewed freeze-dried batches and cultures maintained by regular sub-cultivation) the depositor is again asked to check authenticity. Some collections do not prepare their own batches of animal/human cell lines and will request the depositor to make a new deposit when stocks are depleted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depositors are responsible for authenticating materials and may be asked to provide new deposits if the collection cannot prepare new batches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depositor responsibility to provide sufficient quantity and replacement (IDAC)
rubrics_metrics.description: It is the responsibility of the depositor to furnish sufficient quantity of the material for the specified period. If a culture becomes non-viable or is destroyed during the effective term, the depositor must replace it. The depositary may, for a fee, replenish material on behalf of the depositor, but the depositor must authenticate the replacement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replacement deposits may affect deposit date unless rules for timely replacement are followed (see collection-specific rules about retention of deposit date).

rubrics_metrics.name: Languages accepted by depositary
rubrics_metrics.description: Each collection specifies official languages for communications (examples: BCCM official language English; communications also accepted in German, French, Dutch. NBIMCC official language Bulgarian; communications also accepted in English. IDAC official languages English and French. CChRGM Spanish and English).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit forms and communications in the collection-accepted languages to avoid processing delays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contractual obligations when completing deposit form
rubrics_metrics.description: The application/deposit form constitutes a contract under which the depositor is required to: communicate all requested information; pay required fees; not withdraw the deposit during the required conservation period; authorize the depositary to furnish samples in accordance with patent requirements; make a new deposit if the depositary cannot supply samples; not hold the depositary liable for deterioration if depositor's described precautions have been taken; compensate the depositary for prejudice or court actions arising from handling unless based on depositary negligence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Read and understand deposit forms (BP/1 equivalents) as legally binding; obligations include waivers and indemnities in many collections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Import, quarantine and biosafety regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain microorganisms are subject to import or quarantine regulations. Where applicable, depositors must communicate the species name to enable necessary measures. Collections will withhold potentially hazardous samples until the requesting party proves authorization to handle them. Some collections accept only hazard group 1 and 2 organisms (e.g., NBIMCC).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depositors must contact depositary in advance for organisms that may be regulated and ensure necessary documentation and permits are in place; requesters must satisfy their country's import requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory international and collection-specific forms for deposits and notifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Making an original deposit requires completion of the depositary's application form and the Budapest Treaty model form BP/1 (or collection equivalents). Official notifications use international forms: attestation of receipt BP/4, viability statement BP/9, attestation of amendments BP/8, furnishing notification BP/14, form BP/2 for new deposits, BP/5 and BP/9 for new deposit receipts/viability. Collections may also have proprietary forms (e.g., BCCM/acron/DBT1, DBT2, BP/4 etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preferably send forms before sending material; collections may refuse deposits if forms are not correctly completed. Keep copies and inform patent agents (depositary can provide copies on request).

rubrics_metrics.name: Conversion of previous non‑Budapest deposits (collection-specific rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: Deposits not originally made under the Budapest Treaty may be converted into deposits under the Treaty by the original depositor, subject to storage fees and compliance with administrative requirements for original Budapest deposits (both deposit date and conversion request date are recorded on BP/4). Some depositaries (e.g., IDAC) do not permit conversion of deposits not originally made for patent purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conversion may incur fees and requires completing the same forms as for an original deposit; check the specific depositary's policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Making a new deposit and retention of original deposit date (IDAC specifics)
rubrics_metrics.description: When making a new deposit (replacement), the depositor must complete BP/2 and provide required documents. IDAC: the deposit retains its initial deposit number and date as long as the replacement is viable, made within three months of notification, and the depositor signs a statement that the new deposit is the same as the original.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New deposits may require charges for viability testing; follow time limits to preserve original deposit dates for patent purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Furnishing of samples to third parties — entitlement and safety checks
rubrics_metrics.description: Depositaries furnish samples only to parties entitled under patent regulations. For potentially hazardous organisms they require proof that the requester is authorized to handle such organisms and will only furnish to recognized microbiological laboratories, not private addresses. They may withhold samples until documentation and permits are provided and may require assurances of acceptance of responsibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collections provide request forms (BP/12 or national equivalents) and may assist requesters; requesters bear responsibility for obtaining import permits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification of depositor on furnishing of samples
rubrics_metrics.description: When a sample is furnished to a third party, the depositary will notify the depositor using form BP/14 unless the depositor has waived the right to receive such notification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depositors may waive notification but otherwise will receive official notifications; depositary may provide unofficial earlier notification on request after positive viability testing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cataloguing policy for Budapest Treaty deposits
rubrics_metrics.description: Collections generally will not list deposits made under the Budapest Treaty in their public catalogues. Some collections will list them only if instructed by the depositor or a competent patent office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If public listing is required, instruct the depositary or patent office; absence from catalogs is standard practice to protect confidentiality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Schedule of fees and surcharges
rubrics_metrics.description: Collections publish fee schedules for storage, preparation of batches (e.g., first batch of 20 freeze-dried samples), issuance of viability statements (when test is carried out or based on last test), furnishing of sample (differentiated by organism type), communication/attestation fees, and special charges when depositor must furnish host strains or when special care is required. Fees do not include VAT, transport or bank fees and are subject to change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fees differ by collection and by organism type; special-condition deposits may incur surcharges; consult collection fee schedules (examples given for BCCM, NBIMCC, IDAC).

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance and contact support for depositors
rubrics_metrics.description: Collections advise that depositors deal directly with the specific collection concerned, obtain necessary forms from the collection or its website, and may contact collection staff for detailed information and guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collections provide contact details and staff support; some collections are preparing detailed depositor information packages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance scope and exclusions (collection-specific)
rubrics_metrics.description: Collections list kinds of microorganisms accepted and excluded. Examples: NBIMCC accepts bacteria, actinomycetes, fungi, yeasts, animal cell lines, animal and plant viruses, microorganisms with plasmids but only hazard groups 1 and 2. CChRGM accepts fungi, bacteria, plasmid-containing microorganisms for agricultural/industrial use but excludes animal/human pathogenic microorganisms of unknown nature, mixtures, contaminated cultures, those lacking adequate scientific description; currently does not accept algae, protozoa, human cell lines, animal viruses, hybridomas, nucleic acids and phages pending technique development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check each collection's scope and exclusions before preparing a deposit; curator may accept special-risk items under negotiated conditions and fees.
